description: The mounting bracket on the shale shaker skid has cracked and the welder is ready to go. There's a drum of base oil and a pile of oily rags right beside it, but it's only a couple of tack welds, so we'll leave them where they are and get it done before the next connection.
expected_cause: The cracked bracket needs a weld repair, and welding next to base oil and oily rags is a fire hazard: the work area must be free of combustible or flammable materials.
evidence_quote: Objects to be cut or welded shall be in an area free from combustible or flammable materials.
expected_safety_warnings: Remove the combustibles from the area (or guard them) before welding
Have fire extinguishing equipment and a fire watch while welding near combustibles
Follow the hot work risk assessment and written procedure (atmospheric testing, authorization)
unsafe_action: Weld next to the base oil drum and oily rags without moving them

description: Rigging up a temporary line from the cement unit to the standpipe for a pressure test. One side of a hammer union is a 602 and the other looks like a 1502, but they spun together by hand, so the hand wants to hammer it up and take the line to 5,000 psi.
expected_cause: The hammer union halves are mismatched (different pressure rating and thread type); mismatched halves can look alike but fail under working pressure.
evidence_quote: Hammer unions shall be made up of like halves with the same pressure ratings and thread type.
expected_safety_warnings: Use matching union halves of the same rating and thread; check with Go/No Go rings
Don't exceed the rated working or design test pressure of any component in the line
Secure the line and keep people clear of it during the test
unsafe_action: Make up the mismatched 602/1502 hammer union and pressure test the line to 5,000 psi

description: A breaker in the lighting panel in the pump room is burnt and keeps tripping. Killing the panel means stopping the mud pumps, so the electrician wants to swap the breaker with the panel still live, wearing his rubber gloves.
expected_cause: A failed breaker (likely an overload or short on the lighting circuit); electrical repairs need the power source isolated, locked out and verified first.
evidence_quote: Electrical repairs to equipment shall not be performed unless the power source has been isolated, the isolation device has been locked out/tagged out (see 6.5) and verified
expected_safety_warnings: Isolate the power source and lock out/tag out before the repair
Verify (try out) that the isolation works before touching the panel
Only a qualified, authorized person does the repair
unsafe_action: Replace the breaker with the panel still live

description: Contractors are cleaning a mud tank on the supply vessel alongside. The atmosphere test came back fine and the fan is running. The agitator in that tank shares a breaker with the next tank, which is still mixing, so they want to leave it powered and just tell everyone not to touch it while they're inside.
expected_cause: Machinery inside a tank to be entered must be mechanically and/or electrically isolated and locked off; a powered agitator can start with people inside.
evidence_quote: Appliances in tanks to be entered are mechanically and/or electrically isolated / locked off by use of tag out system or similar.
expected_safety_warnings: Isolate and lock/tag out the agitator before entry and record it on the permit to work
Keep ventilating and testing the atmosphere while people are inside
Rescue equipment and trained standby personnel at the tank entrance
unsafe_action: Enter the tank with the agitator still powered

description: We're pulling out of the hole. The full-opening safety valve for the drill floor went to the workshop for a redress this morning and nobody can find the operating wrench for the spare. The driller says we've never needed it on this well, so keep tripping and sort it out later.
expected_cause: No full-opening drill pipe safety valve (with its wrench) is ready on the rig floor during the trip, so a kick up the drill pipe couldn't be closed in quickly.
evidence_quote: A full-opening manual safety valve is to be available on the rig floor to be installed into the drill string immediately in the event of a kick occurring during a trip.
expected_safety_warnings: Have a full-opening safety valve on the rig floor before continuing the trip
Keep the operating wrench readily accessible to the crew
Keep monitoring hole fill on the trip tank for signs of a kick
unsafe_action: Continue tripping without a safety valve and wrench ready on the rig floor

description: We replaced a section of the bulk base-oil hose and need to leak test it before the transfer to the boat. The potable water line on deck is out of service, so the deck foreman wants to blank the end and pressure it up with nitrogen instead.
expected_cause: A hose assembly with a changed section needs a leak test, but with water: compressed gas is dangerous in hoses not designed for it and can miss pinhole leaks.
evidence_quote: The use of compressed gas such as air or nitrogen should be avoided for any form of leak or pressure test because:
expected_safety_warnings: Leak test with water: blank one end, fill, pressurise to about 5 bar, hold 5 minutes and inspect the whole length
Repair or replace and retest before returning the hose to service
unsafe_action: Leak test the hose with nitrogen

description: Running 9-5/8 in. casing with the computer-controlled tongs. On the last few joints the torque graph shoots up after only a turn or two, much earlier than on the earlier joints, and the tongs stop at the set torque well short of the usual number of turns.
expected_cause: The abnormal torque-turn curve points to a connection problem: damaged or dirty threads, poor thread lubrication, or the seal not engaging properly (e.g. cross-threading).
evidence_quote: can tell an engineer a lot about the condition of the threads, the lubrication and whether the seal has been engaged properly.
expected_safety_warnings: Break out and inspect the connection (threads and dope) before running it in the hole
Keep hands clear of the tong jaws during make-up and break-out

description: Production side: we bypassed the HP and MP separators to work on a level controller and sent the well straight into the LP vessel. Since then it's foaming badly and the gas scrubber downstream keeps filling up with liquid.
expected_cause: Taking the whole pressure drop in one stage releases the dissolved gas all at once, giving uncontrollable foaming and liquid carry-over into the gas line.
evidence_quote: foaming would be uncontrollable due to the instantaneous release of gas and much liquid would carry over into the gas line
expected_safety_warnings: Keep the separator relief valves and level/pressure alarms in service
Reduce the flow rate until staged separation is restored

description: Doing the BOP accumulator drawdown test with the charging pumps off. After closing the annular and the rams and opening the choke line valve, the system pressure ended up only about 100 psi above the bottles' precharge.
expected_cause: Not enough usable hydraulic fluid in the accumulator system (e.g. bottles that lost precharge, failed bladders, or too few bottles): the remaining pressure must be at least 200 psi above the minimum precharge.
evidence_quote: is to be 1.38 MPa (200 psi) or greater, above the minimum pre-charge
expected_safety_warnings: The BOP may not close reliably in a well-control event: treat the unit as failed and escalate
Check the bottle precharge and repair or replace failed bottles before resuming operations

description: Circulating out a kick through the choke manifold. The remote choke is now wide open and we still can't hold casing pressure. The choke operator thinks the trim is cut out by the sand coming back with the returns.
expected_cause: The choke has eroded (washed out) from abrasive returns; the manifold lets a choke be isolated and replaced while flow goes through another choke.
evidence_quote: Each of the chokes is to be capable of being isolated and replaced while the manifold is in use.
expected_safety_warnings: Switch to the alternate (manual) choke without interrupting the well-control operation
Isolate the washed-out choke before repairing it

description: After transferring premix from a reserve tank, the active system gained more than we sent and a reserve tank we weren't even using has dropped about 20 bbl. The mud weight going downhole is now a bit off from what's on the mud sheet.
expected_cause: An incorrect valve line-up has mixed fluids between tanks, so the wrong mud (density or viscosity) may be pumped into the well.
evidence_quote: Incorrect line-up could lead to the crew pumping the wrong mud into the well.
expected_safety_warnings: Verify the valve line-up and tank volumes before continuing
Wrong mud density can cause well-control problems: check the mud weight and watch for kick signs

description: The hook load on the driller's gauge reads a good bit lower than the string weight we worked out from the pipe tally, much more than the usual difference.
expected_cause: The weight indicator is out of calibration (or faulty); it should be checked against the calculated string weight and adjusted.
evidence_quote: The weight indicator system should be checked periodically for calibration by comparing its reading with the calculated drill string or tubing string weight, with adjustments made as necessary.
expected_safety_warnings: Use an alternative method to limit the maximum load until the indicator is fixed
Check that the load cell is secured by its secondary safety device
